query: Prior calculations on concentrated alloys examined variations in atomic mass and force constants, temperature-dependent lattice heat transport, or DFT-derived elastic properties coupled to analytical conductivity estimates; some estimates require a Debye temperature. The cited simulations generally represented perfect, defect-free bulk crystals. Experiments below 200 K indicate that lattice and electronic contributions in HfNbTaTiZr can be comparable, while measurements from 300 to 1200 K on a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen report total conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m). Available analytical approaches do not capture all relevant atomic-scale complexity in refractory high-entropy alloys, and separate transport studies do not establish a predictive solution for this alloy. Given these constraints, what testable hypothesis could an unspecified new predictive approach make for HfNbTaTiZr without conflating lattice and electronic heat transport? Explain why it should outperform earlier approaches, quantify the expected improvement, define its temperature and sample applicability limits, identify supporting observations from the cited work, and specify decisive comparisons with low- and high-temperature measurements that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A physically-informed machine-learned (ML) framework that couples (i) a moment-tensor–potential (MTP) trained on >500 DFT special-quasi-random structures of refractory body-centred-cubic (BCC) alloys with (ii) an iterative phonon Boltzmann-transport solver and (iii) Kubo–Greenwood electronic transport calculations will predict, for an oxygen-lean equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr crystal, a lattice thermal conductivity κ_lat = 6 ± 1 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 300 K that falls approximately ∝T⁻¹ to 3 ± 0.5 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 1200 K, while the electronic contribution rises from κ_el = 7 ± 2 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (300 K) to 9 ± 2 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (1200 K); the total κ_tot therefore remains between 10 and 15 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ over 300–1200 K, matching experiments within ±20 %.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase, equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr BCC alloy; grain size >10 µm; interstitial oxygen <100 ppm; no second phases or porosity.
generation.intervention: Apply the combined ML-interatomic-potential + phonon Boltzmann + Kubo–Greenwood electron transport workflow to compute κ_lat(T) and κ_el(T) for the atomic configuration generated by the potential.
generation.conditions: Homogeneous bulk crystal, temperature range 100 K ≤ T ≤ 1200 K, ambient pressure.
generation.structural_mediator: Accurate ML potential reproduces local force constants and mass disorder, enabling correct phonon lifetimes; electronic structure from DFT captures alloy scattering and electron-phonon coupling.
generation.mechanism: 1. The ML potential transfers DFT accuracy to large supercells (>10⁴ atoms), explicitly resolving mass and force-constant disorder that dominate phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys. 2. An iterative phonon BTE uses these force constants to obtain intrinsic κ_lat. 3. Electronic structure and scattering rates from the same configurations yield κ_el via Kubo–Greenwood, avoiding double counting and keeping the two channels separate.
generation.predicted_outcome: κ_lat(300 K)=6 ± 1, κ_lat(600 K)=4 ± 0.7, κ_lat(1200 K)=3 ± 0.5 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹; κ_el(300 K)=7 ± 2, κ_el(600 K)=8 ± 2, κ_el(1200 K)=9 ± 2 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹; κ_tot therefore 10–15 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ across 300–1200 K and ≈6 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 100 K, with κ_lat≈κ_el near 150–200 K.
generation.baseline: Earlier analytical VCA/debye or elastic-property-based estimates scatter from 2 to 30 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ and cannot separate κ_lat from κ_el; their RMS error versus experiment exceeds 50 %. The proposed method should cut that RMS error to <20 %.
generation.boundary: Valid only for oxygen-lean, single-phase equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in a temperature window 100–1200 K; outside this range or with >0.1 at.% interstitials, second phases, or severe irradiation damage, predictions may fail.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of κ_el depends on assumed electron mean-free-path; impurity levels above 0.1 at.% O or N could lower κ_lat by >30 %; grain boundaries <1 µm would add additional phonon scattering not captured here.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two HfNbTaTiZr specimens: (A) high-purity (<100 ppm O) and (B) intentionally oxygen-doped (~1 wt.% O, mimicking literature sample). Measure: (1) electrical resistivity ρ(T) from 100–1200 K to obtain κ_el=Wiedemann–Franz* T/ρ; (2) κ_tot(T) by laser flash; (3) κ_lat(T)=κ_tot–κ_el.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If, for specimen A in 300–1200 K, |κ_lat,meas–κ_lat,pred|/κ_lat,pred >25 % at three or more temperatures OR if κ_el,meas lies outside prediction uncertainty band, the hypothesis is falsified. For specimen B the model should underpredict κ_lat by >30 %, confirming sensitivity to O; absence of this trend also falsifies the proposed mechanism.
